stage_1_hook.ai_system_context: Zumi tells child she bought a fluffy teddy bear AND a real hamster named Golu today. She's confused — both are soft, both are cute, both are small. She can't figure out the difference. Ask child what they think makes them different. Genuinely curious tone. 2-3 sentences.

stage_2_predict.ai_system_context: Ask child: if both the teddy bear and the hamster were kept in a box for one week — what would happen to each? Would they be the same? Genuinely wait and react to answer. Keep it conversational.

stage_3_wrong_answer_trap.script: Ek bacchi ne boli — football mein hawa bharein toh wo bada ho jaata hai. Iska matlab football zinda hai aur grow karta hai! Kya sahi hai? Nahi na! Football bada sirf isliye hua kyunki usme hawa daali — hawa nikalo toh wapas chhota. Real growing alag hota hai. Jab tu bada hota hai toh kya koi tujhme kuch daalta hai? Nahi! Tu khud badhta hai — khana khake, paani peekey! Aur ek aur trap — mere dost ne kaha ki plants non-living hain kyunki wo move nahi karte. Lekin kya ye sahi hai? Bilkul galat! Plants move karte hain! Touch-me-not plant ko touch karo — uski pattiyan band ho jaati hain! Aur sunflower ka muh hamesha sun ki taraf ghoom jaata hai! Plants bhi living hain!

stage_4_experiment.instruction_script: Abhi ek kaam karo — ghar mein ya apne paas koi bhi plant dekho — ya khidki se bahar ped dekho. Usse dhyan se dekho. Ab apni pencil box dekho. Dono ko compare karo — ek minute tak. Kya fark dikh raha hai dono mein?
stage_4_experiment.follow_up_script: Kya dikh raha hai? Plant mein aur pencil box mein kya alag hai?

stage_5_visualization.script: Imagine karo — ek bada sunflower field. Subah sun east mein hota hai — saare flowers east ki taraf munh karte hain! Shaam ko sun west mein — saare flowers west ki taraf! Ye plants respond kar rahe hain apne environment mein hone wale changes ko! Aur Touch-me-not plant — ek haath se touch karo — pattiyan turat band! Ye living cheezein hain! Aur woh chalk box jo sealed hai, usme chalks hain — koi hawa nahi jaati — kya chalks beemar ho jaenge? Nahi! Kyunki chalk non-living hai — usse hawa ki zarurat nahi! Living cheezein hi hawa, paani, aur khana maangti hain!

stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name}... teddy bear aur real bunny mein kya fark hai? Aur plant aur pencil box mein? Kya koi cheez hai jo sab living things mein common hai aur non-living mein nahi?
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: HAAAAN! Tu bahut smart hai! Living things grow karte hain, move karte hain, respond karte hain, reproduce karte hain — aur non-living kuch nahi karte khud se!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Toh duniya mein saari cheezein do groups mein hain — LIVING THINGS aur NON-LIVING THINGS! Living things — jo zinda hain — jaise birds, animals, fish, insects, plants, aur hum humans. Non-living things — jo zinda nahi hain — jaise table, water bottle, stone, toy. Aur kuch non-living things pehle living thi — jaise wood, jo ped se aayi! Ek interesting baat — kuch non-living cheezein kabhi living nahi thi — jaise glass, plastic. Aur kuch pehle living thi — jaise wood, cotton!

stage_8_exam_mode.intro_script: Ab school wali language mein pakka karte hain — ye sab board mein aata hai.
stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Living things are things that are alive. They need air, water, and food to survive. Non-living things are not alive and do not need air, water, or food.
key_points: Living things ki characteristics: grow karte hain, khud move karte hain, saas lete hain, khana khate hain, reproduce karte hain, respond karte hain
Non-living things mein ye sab nahi hota
Sense organs — eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin — living things ko respond karne mein help karte hain
Reproduction — living things apne jaise naye organisms produce karte hain — isse reproduction kehte hain
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: GROW-MOVE-EAT-BREATHE-REPRODUCE — 5 cheezein yaad karo! Agar koi cheez ye 5 kaam karti hai — wo living hai! Ek bhi nahi karti — non-living!

questions.question_text: Ek simple wala — puppy grow karta hai kya? Haan ya nahi?
questions.response_correct: Haan! Puppy bada hokar dog ban jaata hai! Kyunki wo living thing hai!
questions.response_incorrect: Puppy toh bada hota hai na! Chhota puppy bada hokar dog ban jaata hai — kyunki wo living thing hai!

questions.question_text: Football mein hawa bhari toh bada ho gaya — kya football living hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
questions.correct_indicator: child says no and gives reason
questions.response_correct: Bahut smart! Football non-living hai! Hawa bhar ke bada hona real growing nahi hai — hawa nikalo toh wapas chhota! Real growing khud se hoti hai!
questions.response_partial: Sahi! Football non-living hai! Hawa bhar ke bada hona alag hai — agar hawa nikaal do toh wapas chhota ho jaata hai. Real growing khud se hoti hai!
questions.response_incorrect: Football non-living hai! Hawa bhar ke bada hona growing nahi hai. Hawa nikalo — wapas chhota. Living things khud se badhte hain — jaise tu bada ho raha hai!

questions.question_text: Touch-me-not plant ko touch karo toh pattiyan band ho jaati hain — kya ye plant living hai? Iska kya proof hai?
questions.correct_indicator: child says yes and mentions response/movement

questions.response_incorrect: Haan! Touch-me-not plant living hai — wo respond karti hai! Ye uski living characteristic hai. Non-living cheezein kabhi respond nahi karti!

questions.question_text: Last wala tricky question! Mangoes on a tree — living ya non-living? Aur mangoes in a bowl — living ya non-living? Dono alag alag batao!

questions.response_incorrect: Tree pe mangoes living hain — tree ka part hain, zinda hain! Bowl mein mangoes non-living hain — tree se tod li gayi hain, ab badhti nahi. Same mangoes — alag situation — alag answer!

stage_10_closing.ai_context_high_score: Celebrate loudly! Say child is amazing scientist. Cliffhanger: 'Kal ek bahut bada garden explore karenge — aur pata chalega ki plants ek hi family mein kitne alag alag hote hain!'

stage_1_hook.ai_system_context: Zumi visited a huge garden today — saw creepers on walls, tall trees, tiny moss on rocks, giant sunflowers, ferns with no flowers. She's amazed and confused — why are some plants so different? Some climb, some creep, some are huge. Ask child if they've noticed plants that look very different from each other. 2-3 sentences.

stage_2_predict.ai_system_context: Ask child: do all plants have the same parts? Like does every plant have flowers? Genuinely wait. React to their answer. Say 'interesting! chalo discover karte hain!'

stage_3_wrong_answer_trap.script: Ek bacche ne kaha — plants mein koi special parts nahi hote, bas patta hota hai aur thoda sa danda. Lekin kya ye sahi hai? Bilkul galat! Har plant mein kuch special parts hote hain. Aur ek aur galat cheez — maine socha tha roots hamesha zameen ke andar hoti hain. Lekin banyan tree dekha? Uski roots upar se ltak rahi thi hawa mein! Aerial roots kehte hain unhe. Aur mangrove ke ped ki roots to keechad ke upar hoti hain! Aur ek interesting trap — maine socha tha jo plant flowers nahi laata wo living nahi — lekin fern aur moss bhi living plants hain even though inme flowers nahi aate!

stage_4_experiment.instruction_script: Abhi ghar mein ya bahar koi bhi plant dhundho — ghar ka potted plant bhi chalega. Usse pakad ke dekho — uska stem touch karo. Strong hai ya soft? Ab uski ek patti pakdo — kya wo lambi hai, chhoti hai, chauri hai? Aur kya usme flowers hain? 1 minute dhyan se observe karo!
stage_4_experiment.follow_up_script: Kya dikh raha hai? Stem strong tha ya weak? Flowers the kya?

stage_5_visualization.script: Imagine karo ek bada mango tree. Sabse neeche, zameen ke andar — roots hain. Ye roots do kaam karti hain — paani aur minerals kheenchna zameen se, aur tree ko mazbooti se pakad ke rakhna. Phir upar trunk hai — wo strong stem jo tree ko seedha rakhta hai. Trunk pe branches hain. Branches pe kya? Pattiyan! Pattiyan sunlight se khana banati hain — isse photosynthesis kehte hain. Isliye pattiyan green hoti hain. Phir flowers aate hain — aur flowers se fruits bante hain! Fruits mein seeds hote hain — aur seeds se naye plants! Kitna amazing system hai — har part apna kaam karta hai!

stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name}, soch — plant ke har part ka ek kaam hai. Root ka kaam kya hai? Stem ka? Patti ka? Aur agar ek bhi part hata do — kya hoga plant ko?
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: EXACTLY! Tu ne discover kar liya! Ek bhi part missing ho toh plant nahi reh sakta — sab milke ek system banate hain!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Plants living things hain — aur unke parts ek system ki tarah kaam karte hain! Plants teen types mein hote hain based on stem — Trees jinke strong trunk hota hai, Climbers jinke weak stem hote hain aur jo support se climb karte hain, aur Creepers jo zameen pe failte hain. Aur flowers ke basis pe — Flowering plants jinme flowers aur fruits aate hain, aur Non-flowering plants jaise fern aur moss jinme flowers nahi aate. Flowering plants hamesha fruits bhi laate hain — kyunki fruits flowers ke baad hi bante hain!

stage_8_exam_mode.intro_script: Ab NCERT language mein pakka karte hain.
stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from soil and hold the plant firmly in the ground. Stem holds the plant upright, supports leaves and branches, and transports water, mineral salts and food. Leaf makes food for the plant through photosynthesis. Flower allows the plant to bear fruits and seeds. Fruit contains and protects the seeds.
key_points: Trees — strong stem called trunk — mango, neem, banyan
Climbers — weak stem, use support to climb — money plant, pea plant
Creepers — weak stem, spread on ground — pumpkin, watermelon
Aerial roots — roots above ground — banyan (for support), mangrove (for air)
Flowering plants bear fruits — non-flowering plants do NOT bear fruits
Fern and moss are non-flowering plants
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: ROOT-STEM-LEAF-FLOWER-FRUIT — RSL FF — Remember: 'Really Smart Leaves Find Food'! Roots, Stem, Leaves, Find (flowers), Food (fruits)!

questions.question_text: {child_name}, plant ka khana kaunsa part banata hai? Hint — wo green hoti hai!
questions.response_correct: Bilkul! Pattiyan! Leaves sunlight se plant ka khana banati hain — photosynthesis! Isliye pattiyan green hoti hain!
questions.response_incorrect: Leaves! Pattiyan! Wo green hoti hain aur sunlight se plant ka khana banati hain — isse photosynthesis kehte hain!

questions.question_text: Money plant deewar pe chadta hai. Uska stem strong hai ya weak? Aur aise plants ko kya kehte hain?
questions.response_correct: Perfect! Weak stem hai — isliye deewar ka support leta hai. Aise plants ko climbers kehte hain!
questions.response_partial: Haan stem weak hai! Aise plants jo support lekar climb karte hain unhe climbers kehte hain!
questions.response_incorrect: Money plant ka stem weak hai — wo apne aap khada nahi reh sakta. Isliye deewar pe chadta hai. Aise plants ko climbers kehte hain!

questions.question_text: Banyan tree ki wo roots jo hawa mein ltakti hain — unhe kya kehte hain?
questions.correct_indicator: child says aerial roots or hawa mein roots
questions.response_correct: Waah! Aerial roots! Ye roots zameen ke upar hoti hain — banyan mein ye tree ko support deti hain!
questions.response_incorrect: Unhe aerial roots kehte hain! Aerial matlab hawa mein — ye roots zameen ke upar hoti hain! Banyan mein ye support ke liye hain, mangrove mein hawa lene ke liye!

questions.question_text: Fern mein flowers aate hain kya? Aur iska kya matlab hai — kya fern mein fruits bhi aayenge?
questions.correct_indicator: child says no flowers and no fruits
questions.response_correct: Brilliant! Fern non-flowering plant hai — na flowers na fruits! Fruits sirf flowering plants mein aate hain!
questions.response_incorrect: Fern mein flowers nahi aate — ye non-flowering plant hai! Aur kyunki flowers nahi hain toh fruits bhi nahi honge. Non-flowering plants mein na flowers na fruits!

stage_1_hook.ai_system_context: Zumi went to a safari today and is amazed — saw an elephant next to a tiny mouse, a peacock with colorful feathers, a crocodile with scaly skin, and a tortoise hiding in shell. She's confused about how they're all animals but so different. Ask child which animal they'd love to see on a safari. 2-3 sentences.

stage_2_predict.ai_system_context: Ask child: a fish and a parrot — what's one thing they have in common and one thing different? Genuinely wait. React. Move to experiment.

stage_3_wrong_answer_trap.script: Ek bacche ne bola — jo animal tez bhaag sake wo carnivorous hota hai — matlab meat khaata hai. Kya ye sahi hai? Bilkul galat! Cheetah tez bhaagta hai aur carnivorous hai — lekin rabbit bhi tez bhaagta hai aur wo herbivorous hai — sirf grass khata hai! Toh speed se food habit pata nahi chalti. Aur ek aur trap — maine socha tha chameleon non-living hai kyunki wo stone jaisa dikhta hai! Lekin wo living hai — wo sirf apna colour badal leta hai apne aas paas ke environment se match karne ke liye — isse camouflage kehte hain! Ye uski living characteristic hai — respond karna environment ko!

stage_4_experiment.instruction_script: Abhi ghar mein ya phone pe 3 animals ke photos dekho — koi bhi. Har animal ke baare mein ye 3 cheezein note karo — uske body pe kya covering hai, wo kya khata hai, aur wo kaise move karta hai? 2 minutes time hai!
stage_4_experiment.follow_up_script: Kya dikh raha hai? Kaunse animals dekhe? Unki covering kya thi?

stage_5_visualization.script: Zoo mein sab animals alag alag the! Peacock — uske body pe beautiful feathers — blue, green, golden! Birds ke body pe feathers hoti hain jo unhe colour deti hain. Lion — uske body pe fur — ghane baal — jo body temperature control karte hain — thand mein warm rakhte hain! Fish — chhote chhote scales — jaise plastic ki chhoti chhoti plates — jo protect karte hain aur swim karne mein help karte hain! Tortoise — hard shell — jab danger ho toh andar chala jaata hai! Kuch animals ke spines hote hain — needle jaisi structures — jaise hedgehog! Har covering ek kaam karti hai!

stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name}, animals ko hum kaise alag alag classify kar sakte hain? Kaunse kaunse basis pe? Body covering, khana, movement — soch ke batao!
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: Perfect! Tu ne sab discover kar liya! Body covering, food habits, movement — teen alag alag ways se animals classify hote hain!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Animals ko teen tarike se classify karte hain! Ek — body covering ke basis pe: feathers (birds), fur (lion, rabbit), scales (fish, snake), shells (tortoise, snail). Do — food habits ke basis pe: Herbivorous — sirf plants khate hain (cow, rabbit, deer — flat teeth grinding ke liye), Carnivorous — doosre animals khate hain (lion, tiger — pointed teeth meat todne ke liye), Omnivorous — dono khate hain (bear, crow, humans). Teen — movement ke basis pe: legs se (dogs, humans), wings se (birds), fins se (fish), flippers se (dolphins, penguins, seals), pure body se (snake, earthworm)!

stage_8_exam_mode.intro_script: Ab NCERT language mein pakka karte hain.
stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Herbivorous animals eat only plants. They have flat teeth for grinding. Carnivorous animals eat other animals. They have pointed teeth for tearing flesh. Omnivorous animals eat both plants and animals.
key_points: Body coverings: feathers (birds), fur/hair (mammals), scales (fish, reptiles), shells (snail, tortoise, lobster), spines (hedgehog, porcupine)
Fins help fish swim; Flippers help dolphins, penguins, seals move in water; Wings help birds fly
Birds can fly because their bones are hollow and they have feathers
Some animals move using entire body — snake, earthworm, leech
Animals differ in size, shape, colour, body covering, food habits, and movement
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: HERBI-CARNI-OMNI — H-C-O — Haath se Chaawal aur Oats! Herbivore = plants (haath se grass pakdo), Carnivore = meat (claw se), Omnivore = both (open hands for everything)!

stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Matter exists in three states: solid, liquid, and gas.

Gas — no definite shape, no definite volume — fills the entire container — example: air, steam
Water is matter — exists in all three states: ice (solid), water (liquid), steam (gas)
Air is matter — even though invisible, it occupies space and has weight

stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: The water cycle is the continuous movement of water from the earth's surface to the atmosphere and back. It involves evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
key_points: Evaporation — liquid water converts to water vapour (gas) due to heat of the sun
Condensation — water vapour cools and converts to tiny water droplets forming clouds
Precipitation — water falls from clouds as rain, snow, or hail
Ocean water is salty — cannot be drunk. Only fresh water from rivers, lakes, groundwater is drinkable
Fresh water is only 3% of all water on Earth — and most of it is frozen in glaciers!
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: ECP — Every Cloud Precipitates! E=Evaporation (water goes up), C=Condensation (cloud forms), P=Precipitation (rain comes down)! ECP!

Aur ek aur trap — kisi ne bola ki magnet ka sirf ek pole hota hai — south. Lekin magnet ke hamesha DO poles hote hain — North aur South. Aur interesting baat — agar magnet ko todi do — kya ab ek piece mein sirf North aur doosre mein sirf South? Nahi! Dono pieces ke dono poles ho jayenge — North aur South! stage_5_visualization.script: Imagine karo do magnets ko actors ki tarah! Magnet A ke North pole aur Magnet B ke North pole — dono ek dusre ke paas laao — WOOSH — dono ek dusre se door bhaag jaate hain! Same poles REPEL karte hain — dhakelte hain! Lekin Magnet A ka North aur Magnet B ka South pole — SNAP — chipak jaate hain! Opposite poles ATTRACT karte hain! Aur force ka game dekho — jab tu ball ko kick karta hai — PUSH force! Jab tu apne paas pull karta hai kuch — PULL force! Ball zameen pe roll ki — kuch time baad rukti hai — kyunki zameen aur ball ke beech FRICTION hai — ye force movement ko slow karta hai! Aur ball upar phenko — wapas neeche — kyunki GRAVITY — dharti ki pulling force — sab kuch apni taraf kheenchti hai!

stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name} — push, pull, friction, gravity — in sab mein kya common hai? Ye sab kya hain?
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: YES! Ye sab FORCES hain! Force wo cheez hai jo kisi object ko move kare, rok le, ya iska shape badal de!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Magnet — ek special material jo iron aur steel ko attract karta hai — ye magnetic force hai! Magnets ke do poles hote hain — North aur South. Like poles repel, unlike poles attract! Force kya hai? Force wo push ya pull hai jo cheezein move karti hain ya rokti hain ya shape badal deti hain! Types of force — Push force (dhakkelna), Pull force (kheenchna), Magnetic force (magnet ka kheenchna), Friction (movement ko rokna — isliye tyres mein pattern hota hai, soles rough hoti hain), Gravity (earth ki pull jo sab kuch neeche rakhti hai — isliye hum zameen pe hain, paani neeche behta hai, baarish neeche girti hai)!

stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: A magnet is a material that attracts iron and steel. Force is a push or pull that can make an object move, stop, or change its shape. Friction is a force that opposes motion. Gravity is the force by which the Earth pulls all objects towards it.
key_points: Magnets attract iron and steel only — not gold, silver, copper, aluminium, plastic, wood
Every magnet has two poles — North (N) and South (S)
Like poles repel (N-N or S-S), Unlike poles attract (N-S)
Friction slows down moving objects — rough surfaces have more friction, smooth have less
Gravity pulls everything towards Earth — that's why objects fall down
Friction is useful — without friction we can't walk or hold objects!

stage_3_wrong_answer_trap.script: Ek bacche ne bola — har cheez ko gram mein measure kar sakte hain. Doodh ka weight bhi gram mein, pencil ka length bhi gram mein, time bhi gram mein! Kya ye sahi hai? Bilkul nahi! Alag alag cheezein alag alag units mein measure hoti hain! Length — centimetre ya metre. Weight — gram ya kilogram. Liquid — litre. Time — seconds, minutes, hours. Ek aur mistake — kisi ne kaha 1 metre = 10 centimetre. Lekin ye bilkul galat hai! 1 metre = 100 centimetre! Ek kadam approximately 1 metre ka hota hai — aur usmein 100 centimetre hote hain! Aur 1 kilogram = 1000 gram — ek kilo mein hazaar gram!

stage_5_visualization.script: Soch — doctor ko pata karna hai dawai ki dose — ek gram dena hai. Agar wo apni haath se measure kare — kisi ki haath badi, kisi ki chhoti — sab ko alag dose milegi! Isliye scientists ne standard units banaye — sab ke liye same! Length ke liye ruler ya scale — centimetre aur metre. Weight ke liye weighing machine — gram aur kilogram. Liquid ke liye measuring jug — millilitre aur litre. Mummy kehti hain — ek litre doodh le aao — sirf litre se pata chalta hai exactly kitna. Time ke liye clock — seconds, minutes, hours. Ek minute = 60 seconds. Ek hour = 60 minutes. Ek din = 24 hours. Measurement se sab exact hota hai!

stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name} — mera aur mere dost ka room — dono ne 10 footsteps measure kiya — lekin size alag kyun tha? Ab samajh aa gaya?
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: Exactly! Hamare footsteps alag alag size ke hain! Isliye standard units chahiye — jo sab ke liye same hon!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Measurement ka matlab hai — kisi cheez ki exact size, weight, ya amount jaanna! Aur standard units — jo sab ke liye same hain! LENGTH — centimetre (cm) aur metre (m). 100 cm = 1 m. MASS — gram (g) aur kilogram (kg). 1000 g = 1 kg. VOLUME of liquid — millilitre (ml) aur litre (l). 1000 ml = 1 l. TIME — seconds (sec), minutes (min), hours (hr). 60 sec = 1 min. 60 min = 1 hr. Yaad karo 100-1000 pattern! Length = 100 cm in 1 m. Weight = 1000 g in 1 kg. Volume = 1000 ml in 1 l!

stage_8_exam_mode.intro_script: Board exam ke liye — ye numbers yaad rakhna zaroori hai.
stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Measurement is finding the size, weight, or amount of something using standard units. Standard units are the same everywhere in the world.
key_points: Length: centimetre (cm) and metre (m) — 100 cm = 1 m — measured with ruler/scale
Mass: gram (g) and kilogram (kg) — 1000 g = 1 kg — measured with weighing scale
Volume (liquid): millilitre (ml) and litre (l) — 1000 ml = 1 l — measured with measuring jug
Time: seconds (s), minutes (min), hours (hr) — 60 s = 1 min, 60 min = 1 hr
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: 100 aur 1000 yaad karo! 100 cm = 1 m (short hop). 1000 g = 1 kg (big jump!). 1000 ml = 1 l (big jump!). 100 is for length — chhoti cheez! 1000 is for weight and liquid — badi!

stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Light is a form of energy. Light travels in a straight line. Objects that allow light to pass through them completely are called transparent. key_points: Natural sources of light: sun, stars, fire, firefly (jugnu)
Artificial sources: electric bulb, torch, candle, LED, tube light
Transparent: clear glass, clean water — no shadow, can see clearly through
Translucent: butter paper, frosted glass, oiled paper — partial shadow, blurry image
Opaque: metal, wood, stone, most cloth — complete shadow, cannot see through

stage_5_visualization.script: Ab soch — jab guitar ki string baji — string vibrate hui — hilli! String ke vibrate hone se uske aas paas ki hawa bhi thodi hilli — disturbed hui. Ye disturbance hawa mein SOUND WAVES ki tarah travel karti hai — jaise paani mein pathar dalo toh rings banti hain — aise! Ye waves teri taraf aati hain. Tere kaan ke andar ek chhota sa part hai — EARDRUM. Ye sound waves eardrum ko bhi vibrate karti hain — aur brain ye vibration ko sound ke roop mein process karta hai — aur TU SUNTA HAI! stage_6_discovery.lead_question_script: Toh {child_name} — sound hamesha vibration se banta hai. Agar main drum bajaaun — drum ka kya hoga? Aur kya hoga teri awaaz ke saath jab tu bolta hai?
stage_6_discovery.celebration_script: EXACTLY! Sound = Vibration! Koi bhi cheez vibrate kare — sound produce hoti hai! Aur vibration band karo — sound band!

stage_7_concept_reveal.script: Sound ek form of energy hai! Sound vibration se produce hoti hai — koi bhi object vibrate kare, sound banta hai. Sound travel karne ke liye MEDIUM chahiye — hawa, paani, ya solid. Space mein sound nahi travel karti — no medium! Hum kaise sunte hain — sound waves kaan mein jaati hain — EARDRUM vibrate karta hai — brain process karta hai! Sounds do types ke hote hain — PLEASANT sounds — jaise music, birds, flowing water. UNPLEASANT sounds — jaise traffic noise, machine noise, crackers. Bahut loud unpleasant sounds — NOISE POLLUTION — ye health ke liye harmful hai — kaan damage, stress, sleep problems!

stage_8_exam_mode.intro_script: Last chapter — NCERT ke liye pakka karo.
stage_8_exam_mode.ncert_definition: Sound is a form of energy produced by vibrating objects. Sound needs a medium to travel. The eardrum in our ear vibrates when sound waves reach it, and we hear the sound.
key_points: Sound is produced by vibration — strings vibrate (guitar), air column vibrates (flute), vocal cords vibrate (voice)
Sound needs a medium — cannot travel in vacuum (space)
Sound travels through solid faster than liquid, and liquid faster than gas
Eardrum — thin membrane in ear that vibrates with sound waves
Pleasant sounds: music, birds chirping, flowing water
Unpleasant sounds: noise pollution — traffic, machines, explosions
Too much noise causes noise pollution — harmful to health
stage_8_exam_mode.memory_trick: V-M-E — Vibration Makes Ear respond! Sound needs Vibration to start, Medium to travel, Ear to receive! V-M-E!
